intro: Stoma care protects a person's comfort, confidence and dignity, so give clean, kind, person-centred support and notice and report problems early.
points: Only carry out hands-on stoma care if you are trained, assessed as competent and it is set out in the care plan.
Report a stoma turning pale, grey, dusky, purple or black urgently, as it may mean the blood supply is affected.
Clean your hands and wear gloves and an apron before and after any contact, because gloves never replace handwashing.
Protect dignity and privacy: work in a private space, gain consent, keep the person covered and involve them throughout.
Prevent sore skin by cleaning with plain water, drying fully and getting a good fit, and report leaks rather than re-taping.
Encourage fluids for people with an ileostomy or urostomy, and report signs of a blockage or dehydration promptly.
